subject: Banking
title: Fed Independence Under Pressure
description: A 60-second lesson on Fed Independence Under Pressure.

hook.text: Presidents have publicly pressured the Fed to cut rates.

buildup.text: In the 1970s, Nixon pressured Fed Chair Arthur Burns to keep rates low before the election. Inflation surged to 12%.

discovery.text: Central bank independence means politicians can't force rate changes.

twist.text: Turkey's president fired central bank governors who raised rates. Inflation soared to 85%.

climax.text: Every country that sacrificed central bank independence paid the price in inflation.

punchline.text: Pressure the central bank. Get short-term gain and long-term inflation.

quiz.question: What happened when Turkey's president fired central bank governors?

details.summary: The Federal Reserve's independence from political control is increasingly under pressure as presidents publicly demand rate changes and Congress debates restructuring the institution's governance and mandate.
details.whyItMatters: Central bank independence is considered essential for credible monetary policy. If politicians can dictate rates for electoral advantage, inflation expectations become unanchored and long-term economic stability suffers.
takeaways: Presidents from both parties have publicly pressured the Fed on rates
The Fed's independence is statutory, not constitutional
Countries that lose central bank independence typically see higher inflation

faq.question: Why does central bank independence matter?
faq.answer: Politicians face incentives to lower rates before elections, boosting short-term growth at the cost of future inflation. Independent central banks can make unpopular but necessary decisions like raising rates to control inflation.

faq.question: Can the president fire the Fed Chair?
faq.answer: Legally, the president cannot fire the Fed Chair for policy disagreements. The Chair can only be removed for cause. However, the president appoints board members and the Chair when terms expire, influencing the Fed's composition over time.
